rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Chromatic aberration comes from wavelength-dependent focal length; spherical aberration comes from paraxial–marginal focus separation. Their corrections differ.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Longitudinal chromatic aberration: Δf=|fv−fr|.
For a thin lens in air: 1/f=(n−1)(1/R1−1/R2); n depends on wavelength.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Dispersion Definition:** Dispersion is the separation of white light into its constituent colors (spectrum) due to the dependence of the refractive index $n$ on the wavelength $\lambda$ of light ($n(\lambda)$).  ·  **Cauchy's Equation:** For many transparent materials, the refractive index follows Cauchy's equation $n(\lambda) = A + B/\lambda^2 + C/\lambda^4$. This explains why blue light ($\lambda$ smaller) is refracted more than red light ($\lambda$ larger).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Stopping down does not make glass non-dispersive.  ·  Primary achromatism reduces selected colour separation but may leave secondary spectrum.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Red and blue foci at 20.4 cm and 20.0 cm have Δf=0.4 cm.  ·  An achromatic doublet reduces colour separation; stopping down mainly reduces spherical aberration.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A single lens focuses violet closer to the lens than red, because violet has the higher index and a shorter focal length. The gap between those foci along the axis is the longitudinal chromatic aberration, about ω times the mean focal length.  ·  The working relations are Longitudinal chromatic aberration ≈ ω f and Different colours have different focal lengths. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.text: Longitudinal chromatic aberration is about → A  ·  The cause is → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Chromatic aberration is colour fringing caused by a lens having different focal lengths for different wavelengths. In ordinary glass, blue/violet light is refracted more strongly than red, so their images do not share one focus.  ·  Longitudinal chromatic aberration is the axial separation Δf=|fv−fr| of two colour foci. Transverse chromatic aberration is a wavelength-dependent lateral image displacement, often visible at the edge of a wide field.  ·  Spherical aberration has a different cause: marginal and paraxial rays of the same colour focus at different points because the surface is spherical. It can be reduced with an aperture stop or aspheric surfaces.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Worked case  ·  **Prism Validity:** The formula for dispersive power $\omega = (n_v - n_r)/(n_y - 1)$ assumes small angle of deviation and that the prism is in air. For non-thin prisms or different mediums, angular dispersion depends on the geometry.  ·  A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.  ·  A lens has mean f = 20 cm and ω = 0.040. Estimate the longitudinal chromatic aberration.  ·  Worked comparison: if red focuses at 50.0 cm and blue at 49.0 cm, longitudinal chromatic aberration is 1.0 cm. This is axial focus separation, not a 1 cm sideways image shift.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: An achromatic doublet pairs converging crown glass with diverging flint glass so two selected colours focus together.
